candidates.title: Make the Git diff module own the format its consumers parse
candidates.problem: Git display preferences change diff text consumed as a fixed machine format. Color hides changed ranges; mnemonic or missing prefixes change paths, so the staged gate misses a CCN 8 function.
candidates.solution: Have every parsed diff request a fixed, machine-readable format, independent of user display preferences. Apply that rule to both ordinary reads and prestarted reads. Keep configuration inspection able to read the actual user setting.
evidence: Real Git and gate_staged, ordinary and prestarted reads: default settings produce one violation.
color.ui=always produces no changed ranges or violations. mnemonicPrefix and noprefix produce wrong paths and zero violations.
The noprefix case requires the real path to begin b/. No user Git configuration needs changing.
candidates.deletion_test: Deleting gitio would scatter process flags and record framing across the gate, verify, rescore, mutation selection and history readers. The module earns its place. Deepen its current interface by keeping the diff-format requirements inside the adapter.
benefits: Git owns parsed diff format
Protects gate and changed-file consumers
Real Git settings share one fixture
tests: Add real-Git tests that pass the same staged ccn=8 source through gate_staged with normal and prestarted reads under color, mnemonic-prefix and no-prefix settings.
Preserve nested-root paths, C-quoted paths, Unicode separators, renamed-file handling, literal added +++ source lines and config_value tests.
Check diff_since callers against the same pinned format and cover user-defined diff prefixes/output settings before declaring the family fixed.
candidates.cost: Small change across every diff-producing adapter. Preserve actual configuration inspection and nested-root behavior; do not modify repository or global Git settings.

candidates.title: Let the verdict module own every refusal
candidates.problem: A diff-coverage breach and an eligible gate override take separate decision paths. The override records a successful verdict while the exit adapter still refuses the run.
candidates.solution: Have the verdict module settle all refusal kinds and exemptions before JSON, exit status, ratchet publication and stored-run trust consume that decision.
evidence: Public verify control: exit 6, JSON ok=false, stored verdict=0 and one finding.
With a gate override: exit 9, JSON ok=true, stored verdict=1 and zero findings, despite 13 uncovered changed lines against a maximum of 0.
candidates.deletion_test: Deleting Verdict would spread gate and ratchet rules into more callers. Keep it and absorb the independent breach boolean and final exemption decision into its implementation.
benefits: One owner settles every refusal
Outputs and baseline trust agree
Test all decisions through public verify
tests: Drive public verify with a gate violation plus a diff-coverage breach, both with and without an override; assert exit, JSON, stored verdict and the next trusted baseline together.
candidates.cost: Preserve exit priorities, dirty attribution, storage compatibility and override limits. New test failures and ratchet regressions must remain ineligible for a gate exemption.

candidates.title: Keep execution ownership until every writing process stops
candidates.problem: Mutation locks end with their caller while suites can keep writing. Lane root registration also ends when the root exits, even if descendants remain. A later owner can reuse resources while old processes still write.
candidates.solution: Deepen the execution ownership module so process completion, surviving descendants and resource release share one lifecycle. Lane and mutation adapters should receive the same ownership guarantee, while their measurement and worktree policies remain local. Choose detached-command semantics during design rather than silently changing them.
evidence: Real Windows run_mutants: terminate the caller, acquire its pool again, then the old suite overwrites the new owner's source.
Real Windows run_lane returns after a valid artifact; its descendant later overwrites cov.json under another measurement owner.
Both late writes are proved. Wrong future scores, pool-removal collisions and POSIX behavior were not measured.
candidates.deletion_test: Deleting procs or the helper moves deadline handling, process registration and lock retention back into lanes and mutation callers, so both modules earn their depth. The opportunity is to delete caller-owned lifetime coordination and the mutation-specific parallel ownership rule by concentrating that behavior at the execution seam.
benefits: Execution owns process and resource lifetime
Lanes and mutation share cleanup guarantees
Real crash tests assert resource exclusion
tests: Kill a real mutation caller, then retry while its previous suite is alive; prove no reused pool receives a late write.
Run a lane whose test runner exits before a child; prove the chosen ownership completion rule through run_lane.
Repeat lifetime probes on Windows and POSIX, preserving shell exit codes, deadlines, live-peer temporary fallback, and pool cleanup.

Preserve tests/e2e/test_measurement_ownership_e2e.py; tests/unit/test_measurement_owner.py; tests/unit/test_procs.py; tests/unit/test_mutate_pool_kept.py; tests/unit/test_mutate_nested.py; tests/unit/test_mutate_pool.py.
candidates.cost: Requires Windows and POSIX adapters and PID-reuse safety. Decide detached-child semantics explicitly. Preserve caller-crash protection, fail-fast lane conflicts and mutation's private-tree fallback; longer ownership changes recovery timing.
candidates.adr: None. ADR 0001 concerns MCP argument results; ADR 0002 concerns repository-root selection. Nested mutation roots must still follow ADR 0002.

candidates.title: Make mutation workspace isolation include filesystem identity
candidates.problem: Mutation snapshots follow symlinks, and detached workers preserve their destinations. Writes to a worker path can therefore modify source outside the worker.
candidates.solution: Deepen the mutation workspace module to own filesystem admission and materialization together. Establish how tracked and dirty symlinks participate before any worker write, and make source isolation a guarantee callers can rely on. Choose refusal versus safe local materialization during design.
evidence: Real Windows Git with core.symlinks=true records mode 120000 and preserves the link in the kept worker.
During run_mutants, the suite observes an outside source change from return True to return False; finally restores it.
Caller-death residue, hard links and other reparse points are follow-up cases, not measured outcomes.
candidates.deletion_test: Removing the mutation snapshot moves dirty-test/configuration/deletion capture back to worker callers, so it earns its depth. Deleting an extra helper would not solve the defect. The deepening is to concentrate input identity and safe worker materialization behind the workspace interface, removing the assumption that a path under a worktree implies an isolated file.
benefits: Workspace owns filesystem identity and writes
Every worker inherits source isolation
Real links test writes before cleanup
tests: Track a symlink to an outside scratch source and assert through run_mutants that the outside source never changes.
Exercise relative and absolute links, dirty links, ordinary files and nested roots on platforms that support them.
Assert the selected refusal or materialization behavior before any suite starts, and preserve source bytes across exceptions.

Preserve tests/unit/test_mutate_pool_kept.py: test_every_worker_measures_dirty_tests_config_dependencies_and_deletions; tests/unit/test_mutate_nested.py; tests/unit/test_mutate_pool.py: worktree preparation and cleanup checks.
candidates.cost: Refusal restricts link-using repos; materialization can change build semantics. Choose that policy before implementation. Preserve dirty inputs outside nested config roots and address identity changes between validation and write.

candidates.title: Admit coverage measurements before they become scoring facts
candidates.problem: Malformed finite coverage counters become trusted measurements. Covered branches can exceed total branches, producing coverage above one and negative CRAP.
candidates.solution: Give artifact admission responsibility for valid coverage counts and relationships. Reject impossible measurements with the artifact path and function named, then let scoring keep its simple arithmetic. Check both adapter formats for the same domain promises, while preserving their different attribution rules.
evidence: Public file reader -> score: covered=1,total=2 yields coverage 0.5 and CRAP 10.5 at CCN 6.
covered=4,total=2 yields coverage 2.0, CRAP -30 and remedy=ok. Negative totals can select full statement coverage.
Boolean, fractional and negative counts are admitted. These are malformed fixtures, not evidence that normal coverage producers emit them.
candidates.deletion_test: The coverage adapters earn their place by hiding artifact shape and attribution. Removing them would put format rules into the scorer and lane callers. Remove the unchecked passage from decoded JSON to trusted measurement instead of adding checks to each downstream consumer.
benefits: Reader owns measurement validity
All score consumers inherit valid facts
Public artifact-to-score regressions protect fallbacks
tests: Add public-file-reader-to-score tests for covered greater than total, negative counters, booleans and fractional counters, for branch and statement totals.
Preserve legitimate zero-branch statement fallback, zero-statement invocation fallback, branchless-report warnings and regionless-file salvage.
Keep nonfinite JSON, streaming chunk framing, artifact digests and same-span refusal checks.
candidates.cost: Preserve valid branch, statement and invocation fallbacks; do not clamp corruption into plausible scores. Review ANALYSIS_VERSION implications if accepted measurement semantics change.

candidates.title: Apply the JUnit completeness rule before admitting a lane measurement
candidates.problem: A normal lane accepts a report declaring ten tests but containing one passing testcase. Retry evidence rejects the same XML, so completeness depends on which reader the adapter calls.
candidates.solution: Give the JUnit module ownership of consistent report admission before extracting counts or outcomes. Keep explicit artifact-reuse policy at the lane seam.
evidence: Real run_lane with fresh valid coverage and testsuite tests='10' containing one testcase returns exit 0, one coverage entry, tests_total=1 and no failures.
passed_test_ids rejects the exact XML as an incomplete retry.
Only explicit declared-count mismatch is proved. No full coverage CLI or baseline write ran; missing or consistently false counts remain outside this check.
candidates.deletion_test: Keep normal result admission and the retry guard. Remove the duplicate choice of completeness checks in each reader; deleting either protection loses measurement evidence.
benefits: JUnit owns report admission
Normal lanes and retries agree
Fresh artifact tests cross lane admission
tests: Refuse a fresh normal lane report declaring ten tests with one testcase.
Preserve nested suites, absent count attributes, failed and skipped cases, worker crashes and session errors.
Preserve one-DOM parsing, retry refusal, literal test IDs and explicit artifact-reuse warnings.
candidates.cost: Small local correction can supply the value without a new public interface. Inconsistent producers will begin refusing. Keep absent counts accepted and check deep nested-report cost before reusing repeated descendant walks.
candidates.adr: No ADR conflict. Preserve ADR 0001 tool-result refusals and ADR 0002 root discovery.

candidates.title: Make packet commands use the execution module
candidates.problem: Packet commands use independent shell substitution. A real brief command on Windows expands percent-delimited filename text, targeting a different file than direct test-scoped.
candidates.solution: Delete the packet's second template renderer and publish commands whose execution retains the same exact-argument contract as test-scoped.
evidence: Executing commands.scoped_tests from brief passes src/expanded.py for the literal src/%CRAPKIT_AUDIT_ONLY%.py.
Direct test-scoped passes the original filename. Both commands exit 0.
The packet gate command also contains raw interpolation; that command was inspected, not executed.
candidates.deletion_test: Deleting scoped_test_command's independent substitution concentrates quoting in the execution module. Keep the useful packet interface and its four workflow commands.
benefits: Execution owns literal argument handling
Packets inherit direct-command guarantees
Execute packet and direct command controls
tests: Execute emitted commands through the intended shell against a capture program. Compare received paths with direct commands for spaces, percent signs and supported platform metacharacters.
candidates.cost: Preserve standalone command strings and configured shell semantics. Consumers must not need undisclosed environment setup. Compare actual shell arguments, not rendered text alone.

candidates.title: Give portable records a lossless format owner
candidates.problem: Portable writers emit path characters that their readers treat as record separators. A baseline exported for a valid U+2028 filename cannot be read back.
candidates.solution: Concentrate record framing and field escaping in the portable-record implementation, preserving exact repository paths through export and import.
evidence: Public emit/read control for src/a.py succeeds.
A real Windows src/a<U+2028>b.py baseline exports successfully, then import exits 3: scored row has 2 fields, expected 17.
Ratchet dump/load of the same path fails with one field instead of three.
candidates.deletion_test: The portable baseline and ratchet remain useful independent artifacts. Delete duplicated assumptions about raw lines and tabs, not the artifacts themselves.
benefits: Record adapter owns framing and escaping
Exports preserve repository identities
Public roundtrips cover compatibility
tests: Roundtrip through the public emit/read commands, then ratchet dump/load, using Unicode separators and platform-valid control characters; retain legacy 16/17-column and byte-stability checks.
candidates.cost: Choose backward-read rules before changing writers. Preserve existing baselines, ratchet marks, merge-driver behavior, external TSV consumers and legacy 16/17-column support.

candidates.title: Give duplicate ranking a complete deterministic order
candidates.problem: Duplicate pairs inherit hash-dependent insertion order. The final sort does not fully order both functions, so a tied top cut selects different pairs across processes.
candidates.solution: Make pair ordering total over both functions and the relevant identity fields before applying the requested cut. Keep randomized shingles internal to matching; they must not decide which pair a caller sees.
evidence: Same three source strings, default similarity 0.8 and top=1: seeds 1,3,9,10 select a.py+b.py; seeds 2,4,5,6,7,8 select a.py+c.py.
Both pairs score 0.8095. Only PYTHONHASHSEED changes.
candidates.deletion_test: Keep the duplication module's normalization, containment and pairing rules. Add complete ranking inside that module; deleting it would spread these rules across callers.
benefits: Duplicate module owns complete ranking
Top results remain repeatable across processes
Hash-seed tests expose unresolved ties
tests: Run the same tied-pair fixture in fresh Python processes with several hash seeds, and assert identical ordered payloads at top=1 and without an intersecting cut.
Preserve containment scoring, nested-span exclusion, min_lines admission, twins, process-local index reuse and released source-text behavior.
Include both function identities in tests so equal start lines and same-named functions cannot form another unresolved tie.
candidates.cost: Small ranking correction; a tied result may change once after repair. Similarity values and verdicts are not shown to change. Include full source identities when settling ties.

candidates.title: Make the MCP child adapter read the UTF-8 stream the CLI writes
candidates.problem: The CLI writes UTF-8, but the MCP child adapter uses the Windows locale codec. A refusal containing U+0101 becomes text:null instead of a readable tool result.
candidates.solution: Give the MCP child adapter explicit ownership of decoding the CLI's UTF-8 output and preserve refusals as readable tool results.
evidence: Real Windows CLI prints the no-snapshot refusal and exits 1.
With PYTHONUTF8=0, real MCP emits text:null, writes a cp1252 UnicodeDecodeError traceback, then answers ping.
No hosted MCP client was used.
candidates.deletion_test: Delete the implicit locale-codec decision at this adapter seam. Deleting the subprocess adapter would duplicate the CLI or introduce retained process state; keep it.
benefits: MCP adapter owns child decoding
All twelve tools retain readable output
Real child transport tests the codec
tests: Real MCP child under a non-UTF-8 Windows locale with a U+0101 repo path; require string text with the CLI refusal, no reader traceback, and a following ping response.
Success payload with non-ASCII source paths.

Preserve tests/unit/test_mcp_server.py:57 invalid arguments remain tool results; tests/unit/test_mcp_server.py:277 gate breach remains a result; tests/unit/test_mcp_server.py:350 nearest configuration root.
candidates.cost: Small adapter change and real-process regression. Mocked subprocess results cannot prove decoding. Preserve gate verdict results and argument-refusal behavior.
candidates.adr: None. Restores ADR 0001's readable tool-result refusal contract; preserves ADR 0002 root discovery.

candidates.title: Keep Git path records intact through the Action comment adapter
candidates.problem: The Action's changed-path reader strips names and splits Unicode line separators. Its worklist join drops valid changed files.
candidates.solution: Carry NUL-delimited Git paths through the composite Action and its comment reader without changing their spelling.
evidence: Real Git emits three paths: leading-space name, U+2028 name and plain.py.
The public comment CLI exits 0, reports four changed files and displays only plain.py.
This is a local Git/comment replay, not a hosted Action run.
candidates.deletion_test: Remove strip, splitlines and backslash rewriting from the Git record transport. Keep presentation escaping separate from the path used to join results.
benefits: Action adapter owns exact Git records
Counts and worklist joins stay aligned
Real path bytes reach rendered comments
tests: Actual changed-file record bytes through comment CLI for a leading space and U+2028.
POSIX-only tab, newline and literal backslash paths where the filesystem supports them.
No-base behavior remains separate from an empty changed set.
Preserve tests/unit/test_action_unicode_paths.py:17 ordinary non-ASCII paths; Action comment tests for missing base, missing verdict, finding priority and comment marker.
candidates.cost: Change the producer and reader together and update saved-payload guidance. Keep display escaping separate from join keys; preserve missing-base behavior.

candidates.title: Separate SARIF URI locations from GitHub annotation filenames
candidates.problem: A raw filename is used as both a SARIF URI and a GitHub annotation filename. URI parsing changes names containing # or literal percent escapes.
candidates.solution: Make each output adapter encode the same source location for its own format: a valid URI for SARIF and the correct filename for GitHub annotations.
evidence: Public SARIF builder: src/a#b.py resolves to path src/a with fragment b.py.
src/a%20b.py resolves to a different filename containing a space.
OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.3 requires a URI reference. No hosted upload; the '?' case is synthetic on Windows.
candidates.deletion_test: Remove the assumption that one location string is both a URI and a workflow filename. Keep the shared finding builders and streamed SARIF writer.
benefits: Each output adapter owns location encoding
All SARIF rules share correct locations
Paired formats prevent encoding regressions
tests: Round-trip a SARIF URI to the exact original path for '#', literal '%20', spaces and Unicode.
Build the GitHub annotation from the same finding and assert it still names the original file after workflow-property decoding.
Check separator handling for each supported platform.

Preserve tests/unit/test_sarif.py:27 function locations and :53 changed-line findings; tests/unit/test_sarif_writer.py byte equality, stable ordering and LF output; tests/unit/test_github_annotation_properties.py delimiter and percent escaping.
candidates.cost: Fix both formats together: URI encoding alone changes GitHub file properties. Preserve workflow delimiter escaping, streamed byte ordering and newline behavior.

candidates.title: Let plugin doctor report a failed launcher probe
candidates.problem: Plugin doctor replaces a failed launcher probe with its own version. It reports a healthy installation while the launcher used by hooks and MCP cannot start.
candidates.solution: Keep failed launcher execution distinct from an observed version, and let plugin doctor report the executable and its failed probe as an actionable health finding.
evidence: Real disposable Windows PATH shim exits 7 with no version output.
python -m crapkit doctor --plugin-root <plugin> exits 0 and prints nothing.
Existing low-level tests explicitly expect the fallback, so the regression belongs at the public doctor seam.
candidates.deletion_test: Delete the successful-version fallback for failed or empty probes. Keep discovery and version comparison; deleting them would stop checking what the plugin actually launches.
benefits: Launcher adapter owns probe success
Hooks and MCP share truthful health
Public doctor distinguishes failure from version
tests: Public doctor with a real failing launcher must exit nonzero and name the launcher.
Empty successful output, timeout and unreadable executable must not become a matching version.
Keep a real successful launcher control.

Preserve tests/unit/test_doctor_plugin_root.py:397 compares PATH version; tests/unit/test_doctor_plugin_root.py:410 missing executable is a failure; tests/unit/test_doctor_plugin_root.py:475 successful version output; Manifest, protocol and installed-root selection tests.
candidates.cost: A formerly silent doctor result becomes a failure. Distinguish launcher failure from version mismatch; preserve discovery and successful-version controls.
candidates.adr: None. MCP tool calls to doctor still return an ordinary tool result under ADR 0001.

candidates.title: Preserve exact Git filenames through scope assignment
candidates.problem: Scope assignment rewrites literal backslashes already decoded from Git. Inventory and churn then name different files and the worklist loses activity.
candidates.solution: Keep repository paths exact after the Git record adapter decodes them. Convert user-entered path spellings only at the CLI/config adapter that accepts those spellings, and test the distinction through both callers.
evidence: Pure Windows seam: scan_files rewrites src/a\b.py to src/a/b.py; Git-log decoding preserves the original name.
The resulting worklist row is dormant with commits=0 and risk=0 despite one commit on the original path.
The filename is POSIX-only. No POSIX filesystem or runtime replay was performed.
candidates.deletion_test: The universe module earns its place by centralizing scope ownership and exclusions. Delete its extra interpretation of already-decoded Git path characters, not the module. Removing the module would scatter ownership again.
benefits: Git decoding establishes repository identity
Inventory and churn join exact paths
Cross-module path tests replace obsolete premises
tests: Add an end-to-end path test joining exact Git record decoding, scan_files and churn/worklist selection.
On POSIX, add a real tracked literal-backslash filename test; do not claim the current pure probe supplies that evidence.
Preserve Windows user-argument and configuration normalization at their own adapters.
Replace the obsolete test premise that Git itself emits Windows path separators.
candidates.cost: Needs a real POSIX path test. Preserve supported Windows user-entered spellings at CLI/config seams; removing every normalization rule would break those inputs.

candidates.title: Let the duplicate result limit bound retained pair work
candidates.problem: A top=1 duplicate query retains pair counts and payloads for the full qualifying set before discarding nearly all results.
candidates.solution: Explore bounded candidate retention and delayed payload creation inside the duplicate module, preserving exact scores and total ordering. Measure consumer corpora before choosing a broader algorithm change.
evidence: Synthetic clone corpus, one tracemalloc-instrumented sample per size: 150 functions / 11,175 pairs / 8.824 MiB / 0.135 s.
300 functions / 44,850 pairs / 35.353 MiB / 0.567 s; 600 / 179,700 / 140.880 MiB / 2.655 s. Each returns one pair.
Normal-corpus frequency and production latency were not measured. Timings include tracing overhead.
candidates.deletion_test: Removing the result limit would remove a promise callers need. Removing the inverted index would move cost to broad pair comparisons. Keep both concepts, but make the module retain only the ranking state needed for the requested answer where exact matching permits it.
benefits: Duplicate module owns result-limit cost
Avoid payloads callers never receive
Compare bounded and exhaustive results
tests: Compare bounded results with the current exhaustive result on small random corpora, ties, containment and multiple top values.
Retain clone-heavy peak-allocation and runtime probes; timings currently include tracemalloc overhead and are not production latency figures.
Preserve early source-text release and singleton-owner optimization.
candidates.cost: Prototype and measure before a broad algorithm change. Dense exact matching may still require quadratic comparisons; lower retained memory is the narrower objective. CORE-03 complete ordering is a prerequisite.

candidates.title: Remove conflicting copies of mutation storage guidance
candidates.problem: Current adoption, handbook and installed-skill guidance limit retained mutation worktrees to multiple workers; adoption says a single worker mutates the live tree. The current pool and configuration reference cover all workers.
candidates.solution: Keep the worker isolation, input snapshot and pool lifetime rules in the mutation configuration reference. Shorten the handbook, adoption guide and skill to the action the reader needs plus that link.
evidence: docs/adoption.md:191 claims live-tree single-worker mutation; docs/handbook.html:815 and the skill cleanup row carry the old worker-count distinction.
docs/configuration.md:48 and run_mutants describe the all-worker pool.
Source-backed comparison only; no mutation campaign ran for this documentation finding.
candidates.deletion_test: Delete repeated worker-count implementation details from adoption and plugin workflow prose. Retain the cleanup command and link to one current configuration explanation.
benefits: One reference owns pool lifetime rules
Workflow pages retain only needed actions
Link contracts replace duplicated prose
tests: Check that current workflow guides point to the canonical pool rule and do not assert the retired live-tree behavior.
Do not replace behavior tests with tests that merely pin a new sentence.
Preserve CLI command-table and plugin command contracts; Mutation isolation tests across worker counts; Documentation links and rendered command examples.
candidates.cost: Small prose reduction. Preserve clearly dated release history and useful cleanup commands; do not add a documentation framework for one rule.

candidates.title: Route claim-release paths through the existing CLI path adapter
candidates.problem: Claims release compares the user's raw path with stored repository paths. Unlike sibling commands, it does not rebase the argument after upward root discovery.
candidates.solution: Resolve the release target through the existing command-root and user-working-directory rule before looking up a claim. Preserve the function selector and release-all behavior.
evidence: Handler replay with a read-only fake store: root/src + app.py fails although the shared adapter resolves src/app.py.
Exact src/app.py requests release; ./src/app.py and Windows separator spelling fail.
No real claim was written or released; this is not a subprocess replay.
candidates.deletion_test: The shared CLI path adapter already earns its place across several commands. Removing it recreates exactly this per-command omission. The solution is to use the existing seam in the missing caller.
benefits: Existing CLI adapter owns path spelling
Release matches sibling command behavior
Nested-directory tests preserve discovery rules
tests: Add public claims-release tests from the root and a nested directory, including ./ and Windows separator spellings.
Preserve explicit --repo semantics and refusal for paths outside that root.
Keep exact twin handles, legacy claim handling, ambiguous identities and --all release checks.
candidates.cost: Small correction in an existing caller. Preserve explicit --repo, outside-root refusal, exact handles, legacy ambiguity and --all behavior.
candidates.adr: The correction implements ADR 0002. The current omission does not rebase relative path arguments after upward root discovery.

coverage.disposition: Retain reader-aware cache identity, same-byte hashing and parsing, cold-content sharing and corrupt-row rebuilding. No further cache module change is supported by this review.
Retain occurrence-aware inventory ordering and the shared text decoder. STATE-02 covers portable path framing.
CORE-02 covers finite counter admission; STATE-02 covers portable score records. Retain one artifact walk, strict JSON grammar, nonfinite-token rejection, same-byte digests and same-span refusal.
Retain reader-specific token ordering, module-scope registration for spawned workers and explicit TypeScript syntax refusals. Pygments deferral has a startup purpose and restores its import state.

Retain operation-owned log publication with size/CRC checks and tracked-index cache invalidation. Large-commit filtering and removal of dead paths keep coupling results relevant.
CORE-03 and CORE-04 cover deterministic ranking and retained pair work. Retain early source release, single-target twins, batch index reuse and nested-span exclusion.
Retain shared config admission, duplicate-name refusals and normalized artifact-alias checks. Scope ownership and lane command policy have distinct rules.
Retain strict runtime shapes, numeric ranges and rejection of boolean numeric values. Unknown keys intentionally remain doctor findings to support version skew.
Retain centralized occurrence, twin and claim identity rules. Refusal of unprovable legacy identities protects scopes, marks and claims from silent merging.
Retain the shared FunctionRecord declaration and compatibility defaults. Its small size does not justify moving the declaration into callers.

CORE-S01 affects the path join feeding ranking. Retain debt admission below the floor, evidence-based claim closure and whole-file coupled batches.
CORE-S01 covers exact Git filenames through scope assignment. Retain one ownership rule for scoring and packet routing, including language fallback and open-extension matching.
CORE-S02 covers claim-release paths; STATE-03 covers emitted packet commands. Retain whole-file handles, claim-race fallback and shared batch reads.
EX1 covers writing-process lifetime and MEASURE-01 covers JUnit admission. Retain ownership across execution, parsing and stamping, exact reuse inputs and refusal stamps.
EX1 covers the remaining lifetime gap. Retain platform process adapters, OS locks and explicit console-versus-module invocation rules.
Retain language-aware tokenization and explicit syntax ambiguity refusals. Helper counts and file length do not establish another module opportunity.
EX1 and EX2 cover late writers and symlink escape. Retain ordinary-file isolation at every worker count, captured dirty inputs, stable pool locking and private fallback trees.
Retain the narrow filesystem-snapshot and polling seam. Selection of the initial corpus remains a stated limit; no measured regression supports replacing polling.
Retain the shared suite schedule, installed-source checks and stored-verdict readback. Complete baseline failures, candidate failures and project coverage-context policy remain distinct.
Retain one owner for release versions, artifact identity and retry obligations. The one-active-stage constraint remains documented; no remote release or publication was exercised.
Static package and container checks establish no new defect. Docker execution and dependency-resolution reproducibility remain unmeasured in this review.
Retain generation of operational facts from their owning modules. Deleting the generator would restore duplicated definitions.
Retain real transcript capture and separate GIF/SVG rendering adapters. Demo generation and bundled-font visual fidelity were not revalidated.
Retain the version-pinned coverage reproduction as historical evidence. Its installations and measurements were not repeated or presented as current results.
Retain lazy CLI dispatch and nearest-config discovery. UI1 covers UTF-8 transport, CORE-S02 covers a missing path-adapter caller and STATE-03 covers emitted command quoting.
UI4 covers the false launcher-health result. Retain shared scope ownership, framed runner reports and pure doctor comparisons.
Retain lazy analysis imports, command-family routing and explicit target refusals. The underlying analysis and execution findings belong in their existing modules.

STATE-03 covers packet commands and CORE-S02 covers claim-release paths. Retain exact identity selection, bounded source/context reads and shared budgeting fields.
UI1 covers child-output decoding. Retain CLI reuse and ADR 0001 tool-result refusals.
CORE-01 covers the staged gate's diff input. Retain quiet advisory behavior and the cheap no-config path; linked-worktree sequencing behavior remains an unproved lead.
UI3 covers location encoding across SARIF and annotations. Retain HTML escaping, the report row cap, workflow delimiter escaping and streamed SARIF output.
Retain per-run missing-line ownership and narrow digest values. No additional interface change is supported by this review.

UI4 and UI5 cover launcher health and conflicting guidance. Retain static manifests and the hook matrix required by the plugin host.
UI5 covers conflicting current mutation guidance. Retain documented trust, discovery and recovery rules; historical narratives remain separate from current behavior evidence.
Retain diagnostic prompts and links in contribution templates. PR timing examples are illustrative, not current benchmark guarantees.

Workflow, release and testing tools were reviewed in their execution roles; historical reports, specifications and demo assets were not re-audited as current behavior evidence. Hosted uploads and external publication were not exercised.
STATE-01 covers final refusal ownership. Preserve dirty attribution, named baselines, flake retries and alert/audit-before-grant ordering.
Retain transaction ownership for migrations, claims, overrides and prune protection, plus read-only current-schema opens. STATE-01 covers the verdict fact those trust decisions consume.

STATE-03 covers emitted commands. Retain packet context, source attribution, queue admission and transactional claim fallback.
Retain narrow entry/error definitions and deferred Pygments imports. No further module change is supported by this review.

MEASURE-01 covers explicit declared-count mismatch between normal and retry admission. Retain absent-count compatibility, one-DOM parsing, nested suites and explicit reuse policy; the probe did not run a full coverage CLI or write a baseline.

dismissed.idea: Replace the cache partition module solely because it is small.
dismissed.reason: Fingerprint invalidation and partial-run merging have one owner. Removing the module would move those rules into callers without an established benefit.

dismissed.idea: Cold duplicate inputs are parsed independently.
dismissed.reason: Cold identical content already shares one parse while retaining reader/type identity and separate path records. Keep that behavior.

dismissed.idea: Hashing and parser reads publish records under mismatched source bytes.
dismissed.reason: Analysis workers already hash and parse verified captured bytes. Existing edit/delete race checks protect that contract.

dismissed.idea: The streaming reader repeatedly decodes an incomplete large JSON member.
dismissed.reason: The framing state already waits for a complete value before decoding it. Keep the large-member regression checks.

dismissed.idea: Same-line measured functions silently share coverage.
dismissed.reason: The same-span guard already refuses this ambiguity. Retain its contracts.

dismissed.idea: Remove Pygments deferral or reader registration adapters.
dismissed.reason: Deferral avoids startup cost, and reader adapters supply behavior absent or incorrect upstream. Deleting them would restore cost or wrong measurements.

dismissed.idea: Treat known PowerShell casing/parameter limits, UTF-16 source handling, Rust macro arms and shell substitutions as newly discovered defects.
dismissed.reason: These are documented reader limits. This review supplies no new consumer case or measured parser design that changes their disposition.

dismissed.idea: Persist builtin-hash duplicate shingles for faster warm queries.
dismissed.reason: Python hashes make the index process-local. Persistence would require a stable representation and evidence that it helps.

dismissed.idea: Reopen compressed churn-log concurrent publication.
dismissed.reason: Operation-owned temporary files and size/CRC binding address the known publication race. Retain concurrent-writer regression checks.

dismissed.idea: Claim dense duplicate memory cost occurs in ordinary consumer repos.
dismissed.reason: CORE-04 measures a synthetic clone-heavy corpus. Consumer frequency remains unknown and must inform any broader redesign.

dismissed.idea: Split lanes or release because each has many helpers
dismissed.reason: Removing these modules would distribute policy and failure handling. Function count and file length alone do not establish a missing rule owner.

dismissed.idea: Always force pytest per-test contexts
dismissed.reason: Coverage contexts belong to project policy. Existing contracts cover both configured contexts and their absence, so no default instrumentation change is justified.

dismissed.idea: Treat every nonzero lane exit as an invalid measurement
dismissed.reason: Completed brownfield test failures can still provide valid coverage and JUnit evidence. Measurement admission and the final verdict are separate decisions.

dismissed.idea: Make mutation and file-publication locks identical solely because code is similar
dismissed.reason: Mutation deliberately falls back to private worktrees while shared artifact operations refuse peers. EX1 concerns process lifetime, not cosmetic lock deduplication.

dismissed.idea: Treat release concurrency as a new proved failure
dismissed.reason: The release guide requires one active stage per checkout. No concurrent-stage failure or usage evidence supports revisiting that constraint.

dismissed.idea: Replace watch polling with filesystem events
dismissed.reason: The scandir snapshot has a small portable interface. No measured polling regression supports adding an event dependency.

dismissed.idea: Reject every partially overlapping artifact
dismissed.reason: The current scope check diagnoses zero overlap. No concrete partial-overlap case establishes a separate defect in this review.

dismissed.idea: Claim container delivery or dependency resolution is broken
dismissed.reason: Static checks establish no defect, and no Docker image build was performed. Possible upstream dependency drift remains a risk rather than a reproduced failure.

dismissed.idea: Split cli/admin.py because it is large
dismissed.reason: Administration already delegates root discovery, scaffolding, doctor comparisons and runner parsing. UI4 removes a false-success rule at an existing seam; a size-based split would only move lines.

dismissed.idea: Replace MCP CLI subprocesses with a kept process or SDK
dismissed.reason: CLI reuse avoids duplicated command behavior and retained source/state. UI1 needs a decoder correction; no measured latency case supports replacing the process seam.

dismissed.idea: Add a generalized output framework
dismissed.reason: UI2 and UI3 concern specific Git record and URI rules. A general framework would add an interface while each format still needs its own encoding.

dismissed.idea: Remove the row-based doctor scan used by tests
dismissed.reason: The row-based scan supplies an independent oracle for the counted production path. Moving it offers no established benefit beyond fewer production lines.

dismissed.idea: Rewrite the static plugin hook matrix
dismissed.reason: The plugin host requires individual manifest entries. Their repetition does not create a removable runtime module.

dismissed.idea: Flag linked-worktree sequencing detection as proved
dismissed.reason: The advisory reads .git markers directly, but no public linked-worktree merge replay established a failure. Keep this as an unproved lead.

dismissed.idea: Treat every historical single-worker statement as current documentation
dismissed.reason: Dated upgrade notes can describe old behavior accurately. UI5 targets current adoption, handbook and skill instructions while preserving release history.

dismissed.idea: Split store.py or cli/verifying.py by function count
dismissed.reason: STATE-01 identifies a specific verdict rule to concentrate. A generic file split would leave the same coordination spread across callers.

dismissed.idea: Replace SQLite or add a repository abstraction
dismissed.reason: Current state operations use transactions and named queries. No measured storage limit or second storage backend justifies another interface.

dismissed.idea: Replace ratchet CAS with a long command lock
dismissed.reason: Captured input and a short publication lock detect stale writes while measurement continues concurrently. Retain that separation.
